parameters.jsCode:
// Detection patterns: a column is personal when its NAME matches name_regex or a sampled VALUE matches value_regex.
// sensitivity "special" marks GDPR Art. 9 categories. Edit or add rows in pdi_patterns after the first run.
const rows = [
  ['email', 'contact', 'personal', '(^|_|[a-z])e?-?mail(_?address)?$|^email|mail$', '^[^@\\s]+@[^@\\s]+\\.[a-z]{2,}$', 'email address'],
  ['phone', 'contact', 'personal', 'phone|mobile|tel(ephone)?$|fax|whatsapp', '^(?!\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2})\\+?[0-9][0-9 ()\\-]{6,}[0-9]$', 'phone number'],
  ['person_name', 'identity', 'personal', '(^|_)(full_?|first_?|last_?|sur|given|family|user_?|customer_?|employee_?|contact_?)name$|^name$|^names?$', '', 'a person name'],
  ['address', 'contact', 'personal', 'street|address|postcode|post_?code|zip(_?code)?|city$|home_?town', '', 'postal address parts'],
  ['birth', 'identity', 'personal', 'birth|dob$|date_of_birth|born|^age$', '', 'date of birth or age'],
  ['national_id', 'identity', 'personal', 'ssn|social_security|passport|national_id|id_?number|tax_?id|personalausweis|steuer', '', 'government or tax identifier'],
  ['bank', 'financial', 'personal', 'iban|bic|swift|account_?(no|number)|card_?number|credit_?card', '^[A-Z]{2}[0-9]{2}[A-Z0-9]{11,30}$', 'bank or card identifier'],
  ['ip', 'online', 'personal', '(^|_)ip(_?address|v4|v6)?$|client_?ip|remote_?addr', '^([0-9]{1,3}\\.){3}[0-9]{1,3}$', 'IP address'],
  ['location', 'online', 'personal', 'latitude|longitude|geo|gps|coordinates|location', '', 'precise location'],
  ['salary', 'financial', 'personal', 'salary|wage|income|pay_?grade|compensation', '', 'income'],
  ['health', 'health', 'special', 'health|medical|diagnos|illness|sick|disab|allerg|blood|therapy|medication', '', 'Art. 9 health data'],
  ['biometric', 'biometric', 'special', 'biometric|fingerprint|face_?id|facial|retina|voice_?print', '', 'Art. 9 biometric data'],
  ['belief', 'belief', 'special', 'religio|belief|faith|political|party_?membership|union_?member|ethnic|race|sexual|orientation', '', 'Art. 9 beliefs, origin, orientation'],
  ['criminal', 'criminal', 'special', 'criminal|conviction|offence|offense|police_?record', '', 'Art. 10 criminal data'],
  ['free_text', 'free_text', 'possible', 'note|notes|comment|remark|description|message|free_?text|report|summary', '', 'free text can hold anything; sampled values are checked for emails and phones']
];
return rows.map(r => ({ json: { pattern_key: r[0], category: r[1], sensitivity: r[2], name_regex: r[3], value_regex: r[4], note: r[5] } }));

messageValues.message: You help a privacy team inventory personal data. You see only column names and masked value shapes, never real values. Guess each table's purpose in a few words and mark a column as personal only when its name or shape makes that clear. Reply with JSON matching the requested schema and nothing else.

parameters.content: ={{ '[data inventory] ' + $('Merge The Judge Into The Inventory').first().json.run.summary }}

## Inventory personal data across n8n data tables

### How it works
Every data table on the instance is listed, a few rows are sampled from each, and every column is classified twice: by its name against an editable pattern table, and by the sampled values against value patterns for emails, phones, IBANs and IP addresses. Free-text columns are checked for contacts hiding inside notes. Values never leave the Code node: only a masked shape such as j***@***.com or ##### is kept. After the loop one Groq call sees column names and masked shapes only, guesses what each table is for, and may mark a further column as personal; a suggestion is accepted only if the column really exists and the category is one of the eight known ones. The model can add, never remove. One row per column goes to pdi_inventory with category, sensitivity, confidence, source and evidence; a run row goes to pdi_runs. Special-category columns (health, biometric, belief, criminal) are posted to Discord. Runs by hand or every Monday.

### Setup
1. Add a Groq credential to the Groq node and a Discord webhook credential to the Discord node.
2. Run Set Up Tables once: it creates the three tables and loads fifteen detection patterns. Every other node finds its table by name.
3. Click Scan Now. Open pdi_inventory and sort by sensitivity.
4. Tune Set Scan Policy: rows to sample, tables to skip, the confidence floor. Activate the workflow for the weekly scan.

### Customization tips
Add a pattern row for your own identifiers, in your own language. Column names are the strongest signal, so name columns honestly. This is an inventory aid; a column the patterns and the model both miss stays unlisted, which is why the run row states how many columns were scanned.

## 1. Create the tables and load the patterns (run once)
Three tables with typed columns, or reused if the names exist. Fifteen detection patterns are upserted by key, so running this twice changes nothing. [Data table node docs](https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/core-nodes/n8n-nodes-base.datatable/)

## 2. List and sample
Scan Now or the Monday [schedule](https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/core-nodes/n8n-nodes-base.scheduletrigger/) starts it. Set Scan Policy holds the knobs. Every table on the instance is listed, the template's own tables are skipped, and the loop samples a few rows from each.

## 3. Classify each column
Inside the [loop](https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/core-nodes/n8n-nodes-base.splitinbatches/): name patterns, value patterns on the samples, free text checked for hidden contacts. Only masked shapes survive this node.

## 4. Judge on names and shapes only
The [LLM Chain](https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/cluster-nodes/root-nodes/n8n-nodes-langchain.chainllm/) never sees a value. It guesses each table's purpose and may add a column, checked against the real column list. It can add, never remove.

## 5. Record and alert
One row per column in pdi_inventory, one row per run in pdi_runs. Special-category columns are posted through the [Discord](https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/app-nodes/n8n-nodes-base.discord/) webhook; swap it for Slack or Gmail.
